Author: K. Lakshman
Bench: K. Lakshman
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 Writ Petition No.22210 Of 2024
Oral Order

:
This Writ Petition is filed under Article - 226 of the Constitution of India to declare the action of the respondents, more particularly respondent No.4 in binding over the petitioners under Section - 129 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS') on the request made by respondent No.5 and obtaining bond on 08.08.2024 for a period of one year without following due process of law, as illegal and arbitrary, and for consequential direction to the respondents not to interfere into the cultivation of the petitioners' lands.
2. Heard Mr. Krishna Murthy Devarakonda, learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Government Pleader for Home.
Perused the record.
3. According to the petitioners, there are disputes between the petitioners and their family members i.e., Bonthireddygari Sukendher Reddy and their sisters in respect of lands.

They have also filed a suit vide O.S. No.304 of 2021 against them seeking KL,J perpetual injunction in respect of schedule - A and B properties mentioned therein which are situated at Isojipet Village, Pulkal Mandal,Sangareddy District.

They have also filed an Interlocutory Application vide I.A. No.701 of 2021 seeking ad interim injunction, and vide order dated 27.07.2023, learned Junior Civil Judge-cum-Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Andole at Jogipet, granted ad interim injunction.

entities.text: Junior Civil Judge-cum-Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Andole at Jogipet
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: i) Despite the same, since the defendants in the said suit being influential persons foisted several criminal cases against the petitioners.

In the said process, respondent No.5 made a requisition to respondent No.4 to bind over the petitioners herein for keeping good behavior for a period of six (06) months stating that there are disputes in Survey Nos.76, 191, 192, 245, 289, 293, 175 and 302, situated at Isojipet Village of Pulkal Mandal and that such disputes may lead to disturbance to peace and tranquility of people in the Village and accordingly produced the petitioners before respondent No.4.
In the said requisition, no details of crime etc., was mentioned by respondent No.5.

sentences.text: On 08.08.2024, respondent No.4 bound over the petitioners under Section - 129 of the BNSS by way of accepting bonds for keeping good behavior for a period of one (01) year forcibly, or else to forfeit an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- without following any procedure laid down under law.
On account of the said action of respondent Nos.4 and 5, the petitioners herein are unable to go and cultivate their lands, and thereby their livelihood is being affected.
4. Perusal of record would show that there are civil disputes pending between the petitioners and their other family members.

A civil suit is also pending vide O.S. No.304 of 2021, wherein an ad interim injunction was also granted by learned Junior Civil Judge, Andole at Jogipet vide I.A.
No.701 of 2021 on merits and the same is in subsistence.

entities.text: Junior Civil Judge, Andole at Jogipet
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. However, it is contended by learned counsel for the petitioners that the police have no power to make a requisition under Section - 129 of the BNSS.
There is a procedure prescribed to pass an order under Section - 129 (e) of the BNSS.
The police have not followed the said procedure in the present case.

Even, KL,J respondent No.4 did not follow the procedure laid down under Section - 129 of the BNSS which is corresponding to Section - 110 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973,
while binding over the petitioners herein.
6.

In view of the said submission, it is apt to refer to Section - 129 of the BNSS, which is as under:
"129. Security for good behaviour from habitual offenders.

entities.text: Bonthireddygari Narsimha Reddy vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, there is a procedure prescribed under Section - 129 of the BNSS to be followed before binding over the petitioners.
But, the police without following the said procedure have made requisition under Section - 129 of the BNSS.

7. It is apt to note that Section - 129 of the BNSS deals with 'security for good behaviour from habitual offenders', and the Executive Magistrate has to make an order under Section - 130 of the BNSS setting forth the substance of the information received, the amount of bond to be executed,
the term for which it is to be in force and the number, character and class of sureties (if any)
required.
8.
It is also relevant to note that Chapter - XIII of the BNSS deals with 'information to the police and their powers to KL,J investigate'.

As per Section - 173 (1) of the BNSS, every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, irrespective of the area where the offence is committed, may be given orally or by electronic communication to an officer in charge of a police station, and if given (i) orally, it shall be reduced to writing by him or under his direction, and be read over to the informant; and every such information, whether given in writing or reduced to writing as aforesaid,
shall be signed by the person giving it; (ii) by electronic communication, it shall be taken on record by him on being signed within three days by the person giving it, and the substance thereof shall be entered in a book to be kept by such Officer in such form as the State Government may by rules prescribe in this behalf.

9. Whereas, in the present case, respondent No.5 while making requisition by producing the petitioners before respondent No.4 did not mention the details/particulars of crimes registered against the petitioners except stating that there are civil disputes pending between the petitioners Bonthireddygari Narsimha Reddy vs The State Of Telangana on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111900908/
3 herein and their family members and the same would create disturbance to peace and tranquility in KL,J the village.

sentences.text: Further, respondent No.4 did not follow the procedure laid down under Section - 130 of the BNSS before binding over the petitioners.

In fact, Section - 129 (e) of the BNSS is not a penal provision under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and it is only a procedure under the BNSS for the purpose of securing good behaviour from the habitual offender.
10. As already stated above, Section - 110 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is corresponding to Section- 129 of the BNSS.

In Banala Subhashini v. The State of Telangana 1, this Court had an occasion to deal with the scope and ambit of Section - 145 of the Code the powers of the Executive Magistrate, and by relying upon various judgments of Apex Court, it had held that the Executive Magistrate cannot pass any order, once there is anything to say that prima facie, any person in possession and once there is a civil matter pending.

entities.text: Banala Subhashini v. The State of Telangana 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. In view of the said procedure and the principle laid down in the aforesaid decision, coming to the present case, as discussed above, admittedly there is a civil suit pending in O.S. . 2017 SCC OnLine Hyd. 140 KL,J No.304 of 2021.

entities.text: O.S. . 2017 SCC OnLine Hyd. 140 KL,J No.304 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ad interim injunction order was passed in I.A. No.701 of 2021 on merits and the same is in subsistence.

During subsistence of the said ad interim injunction granted by learned Junior Civil Judge, Andole at Jogipet restraining the respondents - defendants therein from interfering into the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the petitioners over the petition schedule property, order passed by respondent No.4 pursuant to the requisition made by respondent No.5 binding over the petitioners by accepting bonds for Rs.1.00 lakh for good behaviour for a period of one (01) year is absurd.

entities.text: Junior Civil Judge, Andole at Jogipet
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 12. As stated above, there is a procedure prescribed under Section - 129 of the BNSS to be followed.

As per the said Section, when an Executive Magistrate receives information within his local jurisdiction, a person who, habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of offences, involving a breach of the peace, such Magistrate may, in the manner hereinafter provided,
require such person to show cause why he should not be ordered to execute a bond, with sureties,
for his good behaviour for such period, not exceeding three (03) years, as the Magistrate KL,J thinks fit.
He has to make an order under Section - 130 of the BNSS.

Without following the said procedure,
respondent No.4 bound over the petitioners, that too during pendency of the civil suit and subsistence of ad interim injunction.
Thus, respondent No.4 has not followed the procedure laid down under Section - 129 of the BNSS, more particularly Section - 129 (e).

As stated above, if at all respondent No.5 is having any such law and order problem, he has to submit information to respondent No.4 with all supporting documents in accordance with Section - 129 of the BNSS with a request to bind over the habitual offenders in order to secure good behaviour.
Respondent No.4 has to follow the procedure laid down under Section - 129 of the Code by issuing show-cause notice and he shall pass an order under Section - 130 of the BNSS.
But, respondent No.4 did not follow the said procedure.
In fact, in the impugned order dated 08.08.2024, respondent No.4 did not mention the details of the criminal cases pending against the petitioners.
Therefore, viewed from any angle, the order of binding over the petitioners dated 08.08.2024 by respondent No.4 is illegal and liable to be quashed.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the Writ Petition is allowed, and the order of binding over the petitioners, dated 08.08.2024 passed by respondent No.4 for a period of one (01) year pursuant to the requisition made by respondent No.5 under Section - 129 of the BNSS is hereby set aside declaring the same as illegal.
In the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
